In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise testing is a valuable tool in the evaluation of patients with suspected or proven coronary artery disease.
the evidence is strong that the following biomarkers are useful to predict prognosis in heart failure: BNP, NT-proBNP, and hs-cTnT.
the use of biomarkers in the management of patients with acute coronary syndromes has been shown to improve patient outcome, but the optimal use of these biomarkers has not been defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the combination of biomarker measurements and exercise echocardiography provides a powerful means to assess left ventricular (LV) filling pressures at rest as well as during stress.

the relationship between left ventricular filling pressure and biomarkers of diastolic dysfunction in patients with coronary artery disease is complex and may depend on the type of biomarker, the type of exercise, and whether or not the patient has had a myocardial infarct.
there is a strong relationship between biomarkers and filling pressures during exercise, but not during rest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biomarker of the week, the one that has the best correlation with the left ventricular filling pressure, is the BNP.
the relationship of biomarkers and exercise hemodynamics in patients with heart failure is not well understood.
